selector.rationale: High serum hCG and confirmed live intrauterine pregnancy at 24 weeks with a history of abdominal pain and constipation, along with a tender midline abdominal mass, support heterotopic pregnancy as the most specific diagnosis given the evidence of both intrauterine and likely ectopic pregnancy components.

rejected.label: Hyperthyroidism
rejected.why: Undetectable thyroid-stimulating hormone but not directly relevant to current abdominal symptoms and pregnancy findings

rejected.label: Graves' disease
rejected.why: Similar to hyperthyroidism, it doesn't directly explain the current pregnancy-related symptoms and findings

rejected.label: Molar pregnancy
rejected.why: The ultrasonography confirmed a live intrauterine pregnancy, which contradicts the typical findings of a molar pregnancy
